Cause: The cart-service Service has selector `app: cart-service`, but the new 4.2 pods (from the new platform Helm chart template) are labeled with `app.kubernetes.io/name: cart-service`, `app.kubernetes.io/instance: cart-service`, etc. — there is no `app` label at all. Because the Service selector does not match any pod labels, the EndpointSlice controller produces no endpoints for cart-service, so the storefront gets "cart unavailable" even though the pods are Running and Ready. This is exactly the "missing endpoints due to selector/label mismatch" scenario documented for Services [cite: tasks/debug/debug-application/debug-service#does-the-service-have-any-endpointslices-2] [cite: tasks/debug/debug-application/debug-pods#debugging-services-0]. The Service controller continuously scans for pods matching the selector and updates EndpointSlices accordingly, so endpoints only appear when labels match [cite: concepts/services-networking/service#defining-a-service-1].

Evidence:
- Service selector (per ticket): `app: cart-service`, port 8080.
- Pods cart-service-6d5f8c7b9-4hnwq / -kq7rd (image cart-service:4.2.0) have labels `app.kubernetes.io/name=cart-service`, `app.kubernetes.io/instance=cart-service`, `app.kubernetes.io/version=4.2.0`, `pod-template-hash=...` — no `app` label.
- Storefront pods are healthy; cart-service pods Running/Ready with clean logs, which is consistent with a selector mismatch (traffic never reaches them because EndpointSlices are empty).

Fix (owner can apply either option):
1) Quickest: add `app: cart-service` to the pod template labels in the cart-service Deployment (and matchLabels) so the existing Service selector matches again. Verify with `kubectl get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=cart-service -n shop` — you should see the two pod IPs on port 8080.
2) Or update the Service's `spec.selector` to the new recommended labels, e.g. `app.kubernetes.io/name: cart-service` and `app.kubernetes.io/instance: cart-service`, to align with the new Helm chart template.

Either change will make endpoints populate and restore the storefront's cart calls.
